method: k-means on standardised behavioural features (n_init=10, seed 42), clusters relabelled by size

clusters.name: Regular Cash Earner
clusters.description: Account holders receive steady cash deposits and spend most of it through cash withdrawals and household bills, maintaining a moderate balance buffer.
clusters.evidence: 99% cash deposit share, 0.96 spending ratio, median age 40.9

clusters.name: Retired Pension Receiver
clusters.description: Inflows consist almost entirely of regular pension payments, with money spent mainly on household bills while accumulating a deep balance buffer.
clusters.evidence: 98% pension share, median age 71.6, 6.5 buffer months

clusters.name: Digital Inflow Saver
clusters.description: Income arrives almost entirely via electronic transfers into low-earning accounts, maintaining very healthy liquidity and a strong safety cushion.
clusters.evidence: 97% transfer inflow share, median monthly inflow of 2,375.37, 6.3 buffer months

clusters.name: High Volatility Cash Depositor
clusters.description: High volume of cash moves through the account with unpredictable timing, and nearly all funds are quickly withdrawn in cash, leaving thin reserves.
clusters.evidence: Income CV of 0.99, 92% cash withdrawal share, 1.8 buffer months

clusters.name: High Earning Borrowers
clusters.description: High monthly cash deposits are balanced by high spending and an active bank loan, leaving slim monthly cash margins despite strong revenue.
clusters.evidence: 100% active loan prevalence, median monthly spending of 13,593.15, 0.95 spending ratio

clusters.name: Buffered Young Adult
clusters.description: Young account holders receive small, irregular cash inflows and spend more than they bring in monthly, relying on a large existing savings buffer.
clusters.evidence: Median age 21.7, income CV of 1.64, spending ratio of 1.42 with 10.3 buffer months
